verdicts.strongest_argument: The documents this claim rests on are not merely reachable, they are published in the corpus itself: all four appear as indexed items in snapshots/20260830T083607Z.json and in filings.json (F-1 2026-05-27, F-1/A 2026-06-29, FWP 2026-07-21, F-1/A 2026-07-23). More damaging, the hunter's tape argument examines the wrong window. It cites 07-20 to 07-23 (4.46 to 4.53, no volume build) and concludes the market is blind, but skips the F-1/A of 2026-06-29, which EDGAR accepted at 13:22:49Z -- 09:22 ET, before the open. On that session quote.json shows 4.42 (06-26) to 4.18 (06-29), -5.43%, on 72,100 shares against a ~50k trailing average, and the drift continued to 4.14 by 07-01 (-6.3% in three sessions). That -5.43% is the largest single-session decline in the entire 64-bar series. So the market demonstrably does trade this name on its own offering filings, and it priced the amendment on the day it landed -- which is the 70-85 anchor, verbatim. What holds the number down to 60 rather than higher is that the size is nowhere in the corpus: body_available is false, no F-1 or FWP body is stored in docs/, and nothing in the capture states the deal's dollar amount, so the magnitude of the overhang against a $55.5m cap (event.json) is genuinely undrawn. The connection to this specific 09-04 AMC print is also undrawn -- a standing unconsummated registration only reaches the print if management acts on it, and it has sat unpriced for over three months. A second problem is internal: the claim's load-bearing inference is from the absence of a 424B in filings.json, and finding PXS#1 proves that same index is incomplete (it is missing the 2026-03-05 results 6-K entirely, and carries no 6-K at all after 2026-05-26). An index that demonstrably drops filings cannot carry much weight when it drops a 424B, and if a 424B was in fact filed the deal is consummated and fully in the price.

prior_publication.what_it_says: F-1/A accepted 2026-06-29T13:22:49Z, i.e. public before the open of the session in which the stock fell 5.43% on 1.4x volume.
Free writing prospectus, indexed by the 2026-08-30 sweep, establishing the offering was publicly marketed material and not a private fact.
The original registration statement, on the public index and captured in the sweep; quote.json begins 2026-06-02 so its own reaction bar is outside the corpus.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json: 06-26 close 4.42 to 06-29 close 4.18 = -5.43% on 72,100 shares, the largest down session in the 64-bar window, on the F-1/A acceptance date, pre-open. Against that, no reaction in the FWP window (07-20 4.46 to 07-23 4.53, 6,700-34,300 shares) and a subsequent +19% to 5.40 by 08-31, plus the baseline's run_up_5d_pct 16.04 and run_up_20d_pct 23.66 into 6.22 on 09-04, which is not a tape discounting imminent supply. Both readings are in the bars; they point opposite ways, which is why this sits mid-scale rather than at either end.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A stored F-1 or FWP body giving the offering's dollar size -- if it is $10m+ against a $64m cap, the undrawn magnitude alone would justify dropping this below 35.
verdicts.corpus_limits_note: The capture ran n_queries=0 in all four sweeps, so there is no wire copy in this corpus in either direction; silence about press coverage of the offering is not evidence of its absence.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is not a claim priced_in_pct can meaningfully be applied to -- it is a critique of the measuring instrument, not an assertion that the market lacks a fact -- and I say that plainly. But judged as it stands, it scores very high for a different reason than usual: it restates a defect the baseline discloses about itself, in the baseline's own words, in the very file the hunter read. baselines/PXS.json sets event_plausibility.cadence_implausible = true and its reason reads 'inferred cadence of 51 days is too short to be an earnings cadence ... so the 8 matched filings are not earnings -- most likely monthly operational updates caught by the 6-K text matcher. No cadence verdict is possible and the reaction history above should not be used as an earnings base rate. Confirm the date from a company source instead.' baseline_quality adds tier 'partial' and 'thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced.' The claim's own why_not_priced concedes it is repeating this flag. The vol arithmetic is likewise the baseline's published number read back: realised_vol_20d_annualised_pct 65.2 / sqrt(252) = 4.11% per day, and of course a median of eight reactions to non-events (2.33%) falls below that -- that is what the baseline warned about. The one genuinely incremental piece of work here is doing what the baseline asked and naming the real Q4/FY2025 date, 2026-03-05 BMO, from a company source; that is confirmed twice in the corpus (the 2026-03-04T20:49:18Z message quoting the company's own scheduling release, and the 2026-03-05T13:39:03Z message linking the stocktitan results release). The filings.json gap is also real: the index runs 2026-02-19 to 2026-03-18 to 2026-04-01 with no March 6-K, so it is verifiably incomplete. That earns the 8 points between 92 and 100. It does not move any expectation about the print's outcome, and no part of it has a sign.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline is the source of its own refutation here: expected_move_basis is explicitly 'median historical reaction (no usable option chain)', event_plausibility.verdict is 'unknown', cadence_implausible is already true, and options.status is 'not_recoverable_retrospectively'. 65.2 / sqrt(252) = 4.11%/day versus a 2.33% median is arithmetic on numbers the baseline printed itself. No spot, run-up or reaction-history fact in the baseline is contradicted by the claim -- only re-read.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the claim had gone further and rebuilt a defensible earnings base rate -- e.g. sized the actual 2026-03-05 and 2025 results-day moves from bars -- rather than only asserting the printed one is too small, it would drop toward 50.
verdicts.corpus_limits_note: The corpus stores no 6-K bodies, so the claim's assertion that the 2026-02-02, 2026-04-10 and 2026-04-24 6-Ks are non-results filings is plausible but unverifiable here; and quote.json starts 2026-06-02, so the 2026-03-05 reaction cannot be measured from the bars.

interactions: The two findings collide rather than merely overlap, and the hunter's own note that they 'share the StockTwits document' understates it. PXS#0's load-bearing inference is negative -- 'no 424B of any kind appears in the filings index' -- while PXS#1's load-bearing evidence is that this same filings.json is demonstrably incomplete, missing the confirmed 2026-03-05 results 6-K entirely and carrying no 6-K at all after 2026-05-26 despite a print on 2026-09-04 (seal.json, accession 0001493152-26-041540). PXS#1 therefore removes most of the evidentiary weight from PXS#0's central 'never consummated' step: an index that drops filings that exist cannot establish that a 424B does not exist, and if one was filed the deal closed and is in the price. Both also lean on the same negative-evidence move from the same 90-message StockTwits thread (retail never mentions an offering), and that thread is one bounded provider in a capture that ran zero search queries, so it cannot bear the weight either finding puts on it. They should not be summed.
corpus_limits: No tripwires -- tripwire_tells/tripwires is null in all four snapshots, so no document was excluded for contamination and I used nothing outside the capture directory. What I could not check: (1) every snapshot reports n_queries=0 and n_bodies_stored=1, so this capture contains no news-search layer at all -- the only narrative source is one StockTwits thread and its 2-message follow-up, and the corpus is therefore silent, not negative, about whether any wire or trade outlet covered the PXS offering; (2) no F-1, F-1/A or FWP body is stored in docs/, so the offering's dollar size, share count and pricing terms are unavailable and PXS#0's magnitude cannot be sized against the $55.5m cap from anything in the capture; (3) quote.json begins 2026-06-02 and ends 2026-08-31, so the reaction to the original F-1 (public pre-open 2026-05-28) and the last four sessions of the run-in into 09-04 are both outside the bars -- the +15% from 5.40 to 6.22 is visible only as the baseline's aggregate and cannot be attributed to any date or checked for volume; (4) no option chain of any kind, so no implied move and no skew, and I made no run-up-as-proxy argument in either direction; (5) filings.json is internally incomplete as described above, which limits every inference drawn from its absences, mine included.
